plan.topic: A drop of liquid or blood at the injection spot after a tirzepatide pen shot: what the Instructions for Use say it means, and when to call
plan.angle:
08:00 'Is this normal?' practical-moment Short, tight arm.
- Sentence 1 (14 words or fewer): 'Drop of liquid or blood after your tirzepatide shot? Here's what the pen guide says.'
- By 6 s, give the Instructions for Use's own explanation of a drop of medicine or blood at the site. Quote it only if the IFU text loads; otherwise paraphrase without quotes.
- Scope: the US single-dose pen. KwikPens and vials have different steps, so check the leaflet in your box or ask a pharmacist.
- New fact: the label's injection-site reaction rates, 6–8% by dose vs about 2% on placebo.
- Untagged red flags: spreading redness, warmth, pus or fever means call your prescriber. In label wording: swelling of the face, lips or throat, or trouble breathing, means your local emergency number.
- Then the scoped don't-stop line, the Exp F line second to last, 'Not personal advice', the prescriber line and the closing line.
- No doses, missed-dose or technique coaching beyond the IFU.
- Post note: the related-video target is the pen how-to long video (11-11).

package.title: Tirzepatide Pen: Blood at the Shot Site—Normal? #shorts
package.description:
Quick answer: the Zepbound single-dose pen's Instructions for Use say a drop of liquid or blood at the injection site is normal. Press a cotton ball or gauze on it. Don't rub. KwikPens and vials have their own guides.
Spreading redness, warmth, pus or fever: call your prescriber. Swelling of your face, lips or throat, or trouble breathing: call your local emergency number right away. For anything that isn't one of those emergency signs, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.
Sources: Zepbound single-dose pen Instructions for Use (Eli Lilly), revised date as printed on the Lilly IFU, https://pi.lilly.com/us/zepbound-pen-us-ifu.pdf ; Zepbound Prescribing Information, revised 28 Aug 2026, https://pi.lilly.com/us/zepbound-uspi.pdf
#tirzepatide #injectionsite #GLP1
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

script.cta:
Spoken close (Exp F, 08:00 slot, still active on 2026-11-14): 'We answer one tirzepatide question from the research every day. Subscribe if that helps.' then 'Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description.' Spoken total: 159 words, inside the standard arm (135–160). The s4 fix swaps 6 words for 6, so the count is unchanged.

Post notes:
(1) The Studio related-video target is the pen how-to long video (11-11).
(2) Publisher: copy the revised date printed at the end of the Zepbound pen IFU PDF (src1) into its source entry. If the date can't be read, keep 'revised date as printed on the Lilly IFU' and don't make one up. src3 is confirmed on DailyMed as Revised: 8/2026.
(3) src2 (the Mounjaro pen IFU) was removed after a 403 error. All pen-guide claims, including s4's scope line, now rest on the Zepbound single-dose pen IFU only.

factcheck.summary: I checked every claim and found no errors. The Zepbound single-dose pen guide says a drop of liquid or blood on the skin after the injection is normal. It also says to press a cotton ball or gauze on the spot and not to rub it. I confirmed this through a search result that quotes the guide at pi.lilly.com. The PDF itself loads but couldn't be read as text. The Zepbound prescribing information on DailyMed (revised 8/2026) gives injection-site reactions in pooled Studies 1 and 2 as 2% on placebo, 6% at 5 mg, 8% at 10 mg and 8% at 15 mg. That matches "six to eight percent, by dose, versus about two percent" and the 72-week population on the stat card. Spoken words total 159, inside the standard arm. The closing order is correct: scoped don't-stop line, "Not personal advice", prescriber line, the Exp F line (still active on 11-14 in the 08:00 slot), then the fixed closing line. The warning signs in s6 are general safety advice with no source tag, which is correct. They don't tell anyone to stop the medicine, and the label does list serious allergic reactions (anaphylaxis, angioedema) from post-marketing reports. The four issues below are minor: on-screen text that doesn't say whose data it is, an unnamed device in s4, and a source entry with no date. Apply the fixes and ship.

audio.soundNotes: Music already sits close to target (-13.5 dB under voice, -15.3 in pauses); a small +1.15x lift nudges pauses up to the ~-14 dB feel without pushing the under-speech level past -12. Main fixes are SFX density and one loudness spike: the 3.4–3.9s and 21.7–22.3s clusters each had 5–6 overlapping transition sounds during speech, so I muted the redundant swoosh/whoosh duplicates and kept the lead pop/blip/ding/swell per cluster (the ding stays as the clean accent on the 6–8% stat, with no sound added directly on the spoken number). The pop+whoosh pair at 12.0s was a severe outlier at -7.6 dB over voice (nearly as loud as the narrator) and has been pulled down to roughly -17 dB to stay felt-not-heard. The inaudible swell at 4.21s (-53.7 dB) is dropped outright as dead weight. Pause-landing cues (8.5s, 15.25–15.6s, 45.0s) already sit nicely in the -8 to -14 dB pause window and are left untouched. Added two bespoke touches: a tiny injection-pen click under the cold-open blood/needle visual, and a soft reassuring chime near the close to land the reassurance beat without adding another stock swoosh.
